final_report.summary: Successfully implemented subprocess activity detection as a secondary gate in the ActivityAwareHandoffMonitor. The enhancement solves the false-positive handoff problem where LLM sessions babysitting long-running subprocesses (training runs, compilation, data processing) were incorrectly flagged as hung. The implementation uses psutil to detect live child processes consuming CPU before triggering handoff, while preserving 100% backward compatibility when no child processes are present. The design follows gate-only semantics (subprocess check only fires when handoff would otherwise trigger), fail-open safety (all error paths allow handoff), and remains fully model-agnostic. PID propagation flows from atlasforge_conductor.py through ContextWatcher to SessionMonitor to ActivityAwareHandoffMonitor via a clean chain. Configuration is controlled via environment variables (SUBPROCESS_CHECK_ENABLED, SUBPROCESS_CPU_THRESHOLD_PERCENT) with sensible defaults. All 11 success criteria were met with zero regressions across 51 existing tests.
all_files: context_watcher/context_watcher.py (modified: +~100 lines - _has_active_children(), set_monitored_pid(), gate logic in _activity_loop(), updated get_stats())
atlasforge_conductor.py (modified: +12 lines - PID propagation in invoke_llm())
key_achievements: Subprocess gate prevents false handoffs when LLM is babysitting active child processes consuming CPU
Zero behavioral change when no child processes are present - existing behavior completely preserved
Fail-open design ensures safety: missing psutil, dead processes, exceptions all allow handoff to proceed
Absolute max timeout (360 min) remains ungated as a hard safety ceiling
Clean PID propagation chain from conductor through ContextWatcher to monitor
44 new tests (22 functional + 22 adversarial) all passing, plus 51 regression tests passing
Feature flag (SUBPROCESS_CHECK_ENABLED) allows runtime disable without code changes
Model-agnostic: no LLM-specific dependencies, works with any orchestrated process
challenges_overcome: Thread-safe PID propagation across multiple layers without introducing race conditions
Handling zombie and idle child processes correctly (they should NOT block handoff)
Graceful degradation when psutil is unavailable (fail-open to preserve existing behavior)
Testing real subprocess behavior with CPU-burning children while keeping test suite fast (~52s total)
Ensuring the gate only fires at the right moment (when handoff would otherwise trigger, not continuously)
lessons_learned: Gate-only architecture is cleaner than polling: checking subprocess state only at decision points minimizes overhead and complexity
Fail-open is the correct default for monitoring gates - a stuck gate should never prevent the safety mechanism from firing
PID propagation through existing abstractions (ContextWatcher -> SessionMonitor -> Monitor) works cleanly when each layer exposes a simple set_monitored_pid() interface
Adversarial testing with real processes (zombie creation, race conditions, boundary values) catches edge cases that unit tests with mocks would miss
Environment variable configuration with sensible defaults enables runtime tuning without requiring restarts or code changes
